content.user_title: Build Azure AI Projects Applications in Python
content.value_statement: Microsoft Foundry applications require coordinated setup for clients, agents, tools, threads, data, and evaluations. This skill provides focused Python patterns using the Azure AI Projects SDK.
actual_capabilities: Installs and configures the azure-ai-projects and azure-identity Python packages.
Creates authenticated AIProjectClient instances with DefaultAzureCredential and an Azure project endpoint.
Creates basic, tool-enabled, and versioned agents using configured model deployments.
Manages agent threads, messages, runs, connections, deployments, datasets, and indexes.
Starts evaluations with fluency and task-adherence criteria through the OpenAI-compatible client.
Shows asynchronous clients and persistent memory stores for agent workflows.
limitations: Requires an existing Microsoft Foundry project, deployment, credentials, and suitable Azure permissions.
Examples use placeholders and require validation against the installed SDK version.
The package includes only SKILL.md; referenced guides and scripts are not included.
Tool-enabled agents can access code, files, networks, or connected data according to Azure configuration.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Foundry agent
use_cases.description: Create a basic Python agent, send a message, process a run, and inspect the response.

use_cases.title: Standardize project integrations
use_cases.description: Select client patterns for connections, deployments, datasets, indexes, evaluations, and asynchronous resource management.

use_cases.title: Evaluate agent quality
use_cases.description: Configure an evaluation run with built-in criteria for fluency and task adherence.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to authenticate AIProjectClient for {project endpoint} and use the {deployment name} model.

prompt_templates.title: Build an agent conversation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a basic agent that handles {task}, creates a thread, sends {message}, processes the run, and returns the response.

prompt_templates.title: Add approved agent tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure an agent for {use case} with {approved tools}. Explain required Azure connections, permissions, cleanup, and data exposure.

prompt_templates.title: Design an evaluated async workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an asynchronous, versioned agent for {production goal} with memory and evaluation criteria. Include lifecycle, failure handling, and resource cleanup.

output_examples.input: Create a customer support agent using the current model deployment.
output_examples.output: A concise plan covering authenticated client creation, versioned agent definition, thread execution, response handling, and agent cleanup.

output_examples.input: Compare the native Foundry client with the OpenAI-compatible client.
output: Use the native client for Foundry agents, resources, connections, and deployments.
Use the OpenAI-compatible client for familiar chat completion and evaluation interfaces.

output_examples.input: Plan a production evaluation workflow for an asynchronous agent.
output_examples.output: A workflow describing client lifecycle, versioned agents, evaluation criteria, status checks, failure handling, and temporary resource cleanup.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential and grant only the Azure roles required by each workflow.
Keep endpoints and deployment names in explicit configuration, and never place credentials in prompts or source files.
Delete temporary agents and test resources, and use asynchronous context managers for reliable client cleanup.
anti_patterns: Do not enable code, file, network, or connected-data tools without reviewing permissions and data exposure.
Do not assume placeholder examples match every preview SDK release or deployed Azure environment.
Do not expose environment values, connection details, uploaded content, or model responses in logs without review.

faq.question: What do I need before using this skill?
faq.answer: You need Python, an Azure subscription, a Foundry project, a model deployment, valid credentials, and suitable project permissions.

faq.question: Which authentication method does it use?
faq.answer: The examples use DefaultAzureCredential, which can select supported local or hosted Azure identity sources.

faq.question: Can it create versioned agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows PromptAgentDefinition with create_version and a version label.

faq.question: Does it support asynchronous applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It demonstrates the asynchronous AIProjectClient with a context manager.

faq.question: Does the skill execute code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides examples, but users control execution and any Azure resources created.

faq.question: Are all referenced guides and scripts included?
faq.answer: No. The audited package contains only SKILL.md, so referenced files are unavailable here.
